original_card.question: Can one specified masked or overcomplete decoder improve the complete moment budget?
methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound and count all copied information, frames and restoration.

first_step.inspect: Locate the excluded classes: masked identities, at least nine terms, and deeper punctures.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Proof obligation inside the masked (E-graph) model: on which intermediate punctures P112 minus X (|X| = 2..7, i.e. P105-P110) does every rank-<=8 solution of PR1212's system (E) equal D(2G)D^-1, so that decoders with exactly eight costly terms keep PR968's floor 72 - p? Answered by an extension lemma from the P104 frame complements, with an exact census of the punctures it reaches and of what is left.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a masked decoder can beat the floor. PR1212, PR1389 and PR1399 answered it for exactly eight costly terms on P120, P112, P111 and every P104 frame complement, and PR1399 lists P105-P110 as its open next question. This settles the punctures that lie inside a frame and gives a second proof of P111 from PR1212 alone; it does not construct a decoder.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the binding complex supplier: it rules out masked eight-costly-term decoders below PR968's floor on every partial-frame puncture between P112 and P104, so the remaining masked escape routes are nine or more costly terms or punctures containing an odd pair.
stop_rule: Stop at what the extension lemma reaches; punctures with an odd pair (starting with the two P110 orbits) and nine or more costly terms are left as handoffs.
evidence: verify.py: 9 exact checks (E8 model, 2025 frames and W(E8) transitivity, stabiliser orbits of the 1260 frames in P112, the span condition on all 1260 x 16 new lines, the bi-frame cover census, the P111 cover, the P105-P110 table, the odd-pair P110 orbits) plus 5 algebraic checks and controls, about 1 s. Rigidity of the P104 units is cited from PR1212, PR1389 and PR1399, not recomputed.

open_questions.question: Does rank-8 rigidity of (E) hold on P112 minus an odd pair {x, y} (G_xy = +-1), the two FRAME0-stabiliser orbits of sizes 224 and 2688 that make up the rest of P110?
open_questions.why_it_matters: With this package every orthogonal-pair P110 unit is rigid; the odd pairs are the whole remaining eight-term gap at P110, and the extension lemma cannot reach them because no frame contains an odd pair.
open_questions.first_step: For each orbit representative pick a pivot frame inside P112 minus {x, y}, test PR1212's inputs (I3), (I4) on the complete classes and PR1399's Lemma 9 witness connectivity for the lines of incomplete classes, then build the zero-exclusion CNF with PR1212's make_proof.py.
open_questions.blocked_by: Zero exclusion is not inherited: P112 minus an odd pair contains no unit with a known certificate, so each orbit needs its own DRUP proof (python-sat), which no submitted package has.
